methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses convergent lines of evidence: a stress-induced in vitro dormancy model across three prostate cancer cell lines (RM1, 22Rv1, LAPC4), RNA-seq of active/dormant/reawakened states with DESeq2, PCA, TF activity inference (decoupleR/CollecTri), multiple validation assays (Ki-67, DAPI, EdU, DiD, flow cytometry, immunoblotting), siRNA knockdown and lentiviral overexpression, in vivo IIA inoculation with C57BL/6J syngeneic RM1 (with tibial injury and orthotopic spontaneous-metastasis comparisons), PRDM16 subcellular fractionation, ChIP-qPCR with DDK antibody and % input quantification, and correlation with human DTC microarray data (GSE48995) and GSE25136 recurrence cohort. Limitations: small in vivo group sizes (n=3-8 per arm), Student t-test used throughout without formal multiplicity correction, non-blinded analysis, and reliance on a single serum-starvation in vitro dormancy model. Overall rigor is solid for a mechanistic study.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study proposes PRDM16 as a candidate biomarker of dormant prostate cancer DTCs (negatively correlated with recurrence in GSE25136, n=79) and a potential therapeutic target for preventing or eliminating skeletal recurrence - a major unmet need given that 20-50% of patients develop biochemical recurrence within 10 years. Direct translational applicability (PROTAC-style PRDM16 inhibition, RB1 pathway targeting, PRDM16 IHC on CTC/biopsy) is discussed. As a preclinical mechanistic study combining cell lines, syngeneic mouse models, and patient gene-expression datasets, Oxford LoE maps to 5.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE applies for the in vivo components (intrailiac, intratibial, intraprostate, orthotopic). Reporting includes IACUC approval (R7619, R11732), mouse strain/age, group sizes (explicitly reported per experiment), justification for endpoints, antibody RRIDs, software RRIDs, extensive methods detail (siRNA sequences, primers, ChIP conditions). Public datasets cited (GSE48995, GSE25136) and the harmonized prostate cancer resource. Minor gaps: no explicit ARRIVE checklist, no randomization or blinding described, and no statement of a preregistered protocol. Data availability is moderate-good; raw RNA-seq deposition status is not explicitly stated in the manuscript text.

novelty_literature.justification: PRDM16 has known roles in brown adipogenesis and hematopoietic/neural stem cell quiescence and has been linked to tumor suppression in lung adenocarcinoma, leukemia, and papillary thyroid cancer, but a role in prostate cancer dormancy has not been previously reported. The mechanistic linkage of PRDM16 -> RB1 transcriptional induction -> cell-cycle arrest -> dormancy maintenance in bone marrow is novel, as is the simple, reproducible stress-induced dormancy model with IIA inoculation validating phenotype in vivo. The contribution is a meaningful new mechanistic axis rather than a field-redefining discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with clear narrative progression from model establishment, transcriptomic discovery, in vivo validation, gain/loss-of-function, and mechanistic ChIP. Figure legends are detailed and include statistical tests. Discussion is thorough and honestly acknowledges caveats (serum-withdrawal may not recapitulate clinical dormancy, no in vivo pharmacologic PRDM16 inhibition tested, transcriptional heterogeneity across cell lines). Minor issues include long methods sections and some dense supplementary figure references.

key_strengths: Establishment of a simple, reproducible stress-induced dormancy model across three prostate cancer cell lines (RM1, 22Rv1, LAPC4) validated in a syngeneic immunocompetent bone-dissemination assay (IIA inoculation)

Identification of PRDM16 as a commonly upregulated transcription factor in dormant prostate cancer cells, with convergent gain/loss-of-function validation (siRNA, lentiviral overexpression) in vitro and in vivo
Mechanistic linkage to RB1 transcriptional induction supported by ChIP-qPCR mapping PRDM16 binding to -195 to -80 bp upstream of the RB1 TSS and corresponding pRB1 (S249/Th252) activation
Clinical correlation: negative association between PRDM16 expression and biochemical recurrence in GSE25136 (n=79) and inverse correlation with E2F cell-cycle program in patient DTCs from GSE48995
key_concerns: Small in vivo group sizes (n=3-8) and reliance on one syngeneic cell line (RM1) in vivo reduce statistical power
Student t-test used throughout with no formal multiple-testing correction for the many comparisons
No in vivo pharmacologic or genetic PRDM16 inhibition tested after dormancy is established, limiting therapeutic translation
Serum-withdrawal dormancy model may not recapitulate the in vivo clinical scenario; heterogeneity between cell lines (only 14 commonly regulated genes) suggests context-dependence
No explicit RNA-seq raw data deposition statement visible in the manuscript text
chief_reviewer.rationale: Mechanistically novel and well-validated study identifying PRDM16 as a regulator of prostate cancer skeletal dormancy via RB1 induction, appropriate for a strong Tier 2 venue such as Cancer Research or Cancer Discovery research brief, with in vivo pharmacologic PRDM16 perturbation needed to reach Tier 1.
